sql:
WITH order_sub AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.tenant_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.discount_total,
    o.currency_code,
    o.placed_at,
    (
      SELECT s.status
      FROM invoices i
      JOIN subscriptions s ON s.id = i.subscription_id
      WHERE i.order_id = o.id
      ORDER BY i.issued_at DESC NULLS LAST, i.id DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS subscription_status
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.discount_total > 0
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM order_discounts od WHERE od.order_id = o.id
    )
),
rated AS (
  SELECT
    os.tenant_id,
    os.user_id,
    os.order_id,
    CASE
      WHEN os.subscription_status = 'canceled' THEN 'canceled'
      WHEN os.subscription_status = 'active' THEN 'active'
      ELSE 'other-or-no-subscription-record'
    END AS status_category,
    CASE
      WHEN os.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN os.discount_total
      ELSE os.discount_total / er.rate
    END AS discount_eur
  FROM order_sub os
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = os.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = os.placed_at::date
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  r.status_category,
  COUNT(*) AS orphan_order_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.user_id) AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(SUM(r.discount_eur), 2) AS total_discount_eur
FROM rated r
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = r.tenant_id
GROUP BY t.name, r.status_category
ORDER BY t.name, r.status_category

text:
Submitted. Summary of what I did and why:

- Built the orphan set in a single non-fan-out pass: a per-order subquery flags orders (2023‑01‑01 to 2025‑12‑31, `status <> 'cancelled'`) that have `discount_total > 0` but **no** corresponding `order_discounts` row (`NOT EXISTS`), which is the fan-out-safe way to do this since `order_discounts` can have multiple rows per order.
- Attached each orphan order to the status of its most recent linked subscription (via `invoices.subscription_id`) using a scalar subquery (`ORDER BY issued_at DESC LIMIT 1`) — again avoiding any join fan-out — then bucketed into canceled / active / other-or-no-subscription-record.
- Converted `discount_total` to EUR via `exchange_rates` (base EUR, quote = order currency, as_of = placed_at date), treating EUR orders as already in EUR.
- Aggregated to tenant × status_category with order count, distinct customers, and EUR discount total, ordered by tenant then category.

Flagged two caveats in the note: I had to infer the "orphan" definition since the earlier 2025-only request wasn't visible to me in this session, and as the engineer I never see query output (dry_run uses an empty schema), so I can't personally verify the ~1,188 orders / ~€57,658.66 reconciliation — that comparison needs to happen once the analyst has the printed report.
